- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.68 → 82.31) by overreacting to recent volatility.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — model holds too much upward bias after peaks.
- Lags in correcting downward trends — model takes longer to recognize and respond to price corrections.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the final 5–10 days, especially when true prices show downward momentum.
- Model exhibits “sticky” bias — once a price spike occurs, it fails to adjust downward quickly, even if historical data suggests mean reversion.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent high values — model “follows” recent peaks rather than smoothing or averaging.
